course.title: Critical reading workshop
course.description: Synthetic course for local interface review. No real student records or original teaching materials.

sessions.title: Evidence, argument & interpretation
sessions.subtitle: Read closely, question assumptions, and build an evidence-based response.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a claim from supporting evidence.
sessions.instructions: Offer concise formative guidance and encourage students to explain their reasoning.

groups.title: Core questions
groups.description: Complete all questions in this group.

questions.prompt: What is the central claim in the reading? Explain it in your own words.
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between a claim and evidence?
options: Evidence provides support for a claim.
A claim and evidence are always identical.
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

questions.prompt: Identify one piece of evidence and explain how it supports the argument.
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

questions.prompt: How might the intended audience influence the language used in this source?
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

questions.prompt: Compare two possible interpretations of the reading. What supports each interpretation?
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

questions.prompt: What further question would help you evaluate the argument? Explain why.
questions.hint: Distinguish what the text says from what you infer.

materials.title: Reading critically: claims and evidence
materials.excerpt: A claim describes what an author believes. Evidence supports a claim, while interpretation explains why that evidence matters.

sessions.title: Reading different perspectives
sessions.subtitle: Understand how context shapes a source.
learning_objectives: Explain how audience and context shape an argument.
